A second, separate discrepancy: the GT-packages source describing 'Rally Package' contents for GT states it includes 'Oxford White interior trim,' while Ford's own 2026 what's-new notes and a dedicated Ford Authority article both state the Oxford White seatback/seat trim was REMOVED for 2026 and is 'no longer available... even as an option.' discrepancy_notes: CRITICAL: ford.com's own Escape model pages (Active, ST-Line, Platinum, etc.) do not render normal spec content at all -- every one fetched returns only a discontinuation banner ('Ford Escape Is Tapping the Brakes... we're discontinuing the Ford Escape for the time being') plus a footnote: '2026 Escape unavailable for purchase in CA, MA, OR, NY, WA, and VT.' This is a live, current confirmation from Ford's own site, not just older news coverage. Ford Authority (June 2025) separately reported the same six-state exclusion, tied to the 2026 Escape only being certified with the non-California emissions standard. Most trade coverage (J.D. Power, Ford Authority, dealer sites) describes 2026 as the Escape's FINAL model year, with Louisville Assembly retooling for an EV, though Ford has not issued a formal end-of-production statement in the sources found; Ford.com's own current framing ('discontinuing... for the time being') is softer than 'final model year' and leaves open an ambiguous status. Both are reported here rather than asserting one as fact. Ford Authority (June 2025, pre-production) said ST-Line and Platinum would drop their FWD-hybrid option for 2026 (AWD-only hybrid); Edmunds' trim/pricing data (checked post-launch) is consistent with this -- it lists ST-Line Select/Elite and Platinum hybrid trims as AWD-only, with no FWD hybrid line. Dealer-template sites (astroford.com) used as last-resort, flagged sources for ST-Line Select/Elite/PHEV show internal contradictions within their own pages (e.g., listing both $38,705 and $30,350 as ST-Line Elite's MSRP in different sections, and conflicting wheel/seat-material descriptions between their 'features' list and 'comparison table') -- these conflicts are noted and the more specific, trim-named figures were used over the generic ones that duplicate the Active trim's numbers. Exterior color lists conflict across sources: Ford Authority's dedicated color article (6 retail colors: Carbonized Gray, Space Silver, Agate Black standard; Vapor Blue, Rapid Red +$495; Star White Tri-Coat +$995, plus fleet-only Oxford White on Active) disagrees with both astroford.com's dealer-template list (Oxford White/Agate Black standard; Carbonized Gray/Iconic Silver/Atlas Blue +$495; Star White/Rapid Red +$595) and cars.com's Active-trim list (which includes 'Light Blue Metallic' and 'Bright Silver,' names found nowhere else). Ford Authority's article was treated as the most likely accurate Ford-order-guide-based source and used in this dataset; the conflicting lists are flagged rather than merged or guessed between.
confidence_notes: Ford.com's Escape section currently serves a discontinuation banner instead of the JS Build & Price tool/spec pages, so ZERO ford.com trim-level spec data (colors, wheels, roofs, seating, packages) could be gathered directly from Ford's own site for any Escape trim -- this is a materially different (and more severe) failure mode than the 'JS SPA renders placeholders' issue seen on Maverick/Bronco Sport, and likely reflects Escape's discontinued/restricted-sale status rather than a technical fetch problem. All Escape trim-level detail below is therefore sourced from Edmunds (secondary, as instructed) plus Ford Authority's Ford-order-guide-based articles (colors, packages, wheels, pricing-change coverage), with dealer-template sites (astroford.com) used only as a last resort for ST-Line Select/Elite/PHEV trim specifics, flagged accordingly. Base MSRP is not a required column but is noted in discrepancy_notes context where relevant; it was likewise inconsistent across sources (Edmunds vs. Ford Authority vs. astroford) for several trims.
